key_insight: Targeted repair can improve trustworthiness in distilled language models while largely preserving capabilities inherited from the teacher.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical alternative to re-distillation when the original distillation corpus is unavailable.
method: Use a proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) to constrain changes during repair.
Estimate the required curvature using a surrogate proxy dataset.
Incorporate preferred and dispreferred response pairs through an odds-ratio objective.
evidence_signal: Across different distilled models in pre-training and post-training settings, the abstract reports trustworthiness improvements of up to 8% with less than 1% decrement in perplexity.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify proxy-dataset sensitivity or whether the reported perplexity decrement denotes improvement or degradation.
paper_title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
